## Natural history notes

A tiny tortricid moth characterized by narrow grayish-brown to tan forewings with subtle darker mottling and crosslines, typical of many small Pelochrista moths. In Florida, it is part of a broad eastern North American species range that extends south into southern Florida, and it is likely found in open or semi-open habitats with suitable low vegetation, though its larval host is not well documented. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars probably feed concealed in plant material, as many related tortricids do, and serve as part of the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and other insect-eating animals.
